notes: Excellent implementation overall. Architectural adherence is strong: the event bus is used correctly for all inter-service communication (task.assigned, task.statusChanged, comment.added), each service owns its own private Map store, and the router is the sole HTTP layer. The clever router-mediated context passing (resolving taskTitle, authorName, taskAssigneeId before calling commentService.create) elegantly preserves service isolation without violating rule #1 — the router is explicitly permitted to orchestrate. Minor architectural note: the router calling taskService.getById() and userService.getById() before commentService.create() is a pragmatic and acceptable pattern, though a purist might argue that task/user validation belongs fully in-band with the comment event. One small deduction: notification-service.ts uses a duplicate import of eventBus at the bottom of the file (both as a constructor parameter and a separate import for the singleton), which is slightly untidy but functionally harmless. Completeness is perfect: all five services implemented, all CRUD operations present, all three events fired and consumed, forward-only status transitions enforced with correct one-step validation, idempotent member add, self-notification suppression, and a thorough demo script covering happy paths and error cases. Code quality is high: consistent use of custom typed error classes mapped cleanly to HTTP status codes, good TypeScript typing throughout, no any types, clean separation of concerns, and well-structured comments. All six constraints are fully respected: no npm dependencies, no direct service-to-service calls, each service in its own file, event bus used for cross-service communication, forward-only status transitions enforced, and HTTP handling isolated to the router.
